diagram_candidates.certainty: focused editorial candidate; the proof is mathematically complete in text
diagram_candidates.excerpt: Lift a nullhomotopy with the given loop as its initial edge; uniqueness forces the opposite edge to be constant.
diagram_candidates.maps_and_check: Show the square I×I downstairs with the nullhomotopy H on its base edge and constant side/opposite edges; lift H through p:E→B from the loop α upstairs. Mark p∘α=β and the lifted boundary. Homotopy-lifting uniqueness forces the lifted opposite edge to be constant at e₀, so α is nullhomotopic.
diagram_candidates.reason: A square makes the boundary conditions and the exact use of uniqueness immediate, clarifying the short lifting argument without carrying proof responsibility.

diagram_candidates.certainty: focused editorial candidate; use schematic drawings with the stated polygonal/Jordan hypotheses
diagram_candidates.excerpt: The crosscut claim and ear induction split one face along an arc whose endpoints lie on its boundary cycle.
diagram_candidates.maps_and_check: Draw a face F bounded by cycle J and an added ear Q from u to v with interior in F. Split J into J₁,J₂; mark Dᵢ=Jᵢ∪Q and the two resulting regions Y₁,Y₂. Check that D₁,D₂ are Jordan graph cycles, F\Q=Y₁⊔Y₂, and adding a k-edge ear changes (V,E,F) by (k−1,k,1), preserving V−E+F. For the hybrid case, distinguish the exterior face that remains unchanged.
diagram_candidates.reason: The long crosscut and face-induction prose tracks two boundary cycles, complementary regions, and their frontiers; a carefully labelled figure would make the split and invariant easier to follow. The text remains the proof.
